subject: Acme Retail — post-demo architecture notes & next actions (SDK/auth/routing)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Retail — post-demo architecture notes & next actions (SDK/auth/routing)

Hi Liam — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs (what you confirmed on the call):
- In-app customer support assistant (chat + tool-calling to query order system)
- High-throughput embedding search for product recommendations and re-ranker for top-N results
- Multi-region latency targets (US East for checkout, EU for EU customers), failover to lower-cost model when capacity constrained
- Strict data separation for PII (redaction + KMS) and SOC2 evidence for procurement

Architecture items we discussed to validate:
1) SDK & auth: you prefer server-side SDK integration with API keys from a dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool; procurement asked about mTLS and SCIM for automated key rotation.
2) Routing & policy: route production checkout traffic to a low-latency model variant in us-east, with a cost-policy that triggers quantized fallback after 120ms 99th percentile or when spend budget threshold is hit.
3) Structured output/tool-calling: the assistant needs to call your orders API (POST /orders/query) and return structured JSON (order_id, status, fulfillment_eta). We suggested Redwood function-calls + webhook proxy.
4) Embeddings & reranker: periodic offline embed builds (daily) with upsert into a vectorstore; online rerank at request time using a small cross-encoder.

Attachments: draft integration proposal, auth requirements spreadsheet, minimal webhook spec (attached).

Proposed immediate next steps (we can slot these in this week):
- Action A (Priyom): Share a short tech checklist and the proposal (attached).
- Action B (Ben): Provide recommended SDK snippets (Node + Python) and a sample fallback policy JSON for your engineers to review.
- Action C (Kimberly): Start procurement packet (SOC2 template + customer encryption notes) and confirm if mTLS is required vs. KMS-only.
- Action D (Liam): Confirm who from your infra/procurement team should be included and whether we should run a 60-minute technical sandbox session.

If that matches your read, I can set up the sandbox session and loop in our infra SE for a deep-dive on routing and failover.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0113

Subject: Re: Acme Retail — post-demo architecture notes & next actions (SDK/auth/routing)

Thanks Priyom — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) mTLS vs KMS: procurement prefers mTLS for service-to-service for now; they will still want KMS for customer data encryption at rest. Is mTLS supported in the Private deployment flow?
2) Failover policy: can the fallback chain include a regional model (eu-west) and then a quantized cheaper variant in the same region? Our regulatory team wants EU customer data routed within EU unless failover is needed.
3) Tool calling: we can expose a read-only orders proxy endpoint specifically for Redwood. We'll need a sample contract/schema for that route.

Yes please include our infra lead (cc'd: procurement) and let's do the sandbox next Thursday if that works for your SE.

-Liam
Director, Product Engineering | Acme Retail
liam.oconnor@acme-retail.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-retail.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Retail — post-demo architecture notes & next actions (SDK/auth/routing)

Liam — quick technical notes answering your questions. I'm Ben (Solutions Engineer), I'll run the sandbox with you.

mTLS & Private: Yes — Redwood Private supports mTLS termination on the customer side with cert-based auth to the data plane. For hosted Dedicated we can support mTLS to a fronting proxy; if you require full end-to-end cert control we recommend our Private (VPC) deployment. I'll attach an auth capabilities matrix to the procurement packet.

Regional failover & policy: You can configure routing rules like: region_priority = [eu-west, eu-central, us-east] and then attach model variants + quantization level to each priority. Failover chain example we recommend:
- Primary: eu-west high perf (latency SLO 80ms p95)
- Secondary: eu-west quantized (cost-saving)
- Tertiary: us-east low-cost (only if explicit cross-region allowed)
We can enforce per-route data residency constraints so EU customer tokens never route cross-region unless you opt-in.

Tool calling / structured output: see embedded spec in the attached webhook-and-tooling-spec.json — we support function-call style JSON with a strict schema enforcement option (we can return 400 if payload deviates). For your orders API we'll recommend a typed contract and a pre-flight sandbox that can validate schemas automatically.

Embeddings / re-rank: Operational pattern we've used: daily offline embed jobs (batch job with upserts), a lightweight vector DB (managed) for ANN, and a cross-encoder served at low QPS for reranking top-50. We'll send an example config for batch windowing and memory/KV sizing.

I'll prepare: SDK snippets (node/python), a sample routing policy JSON, and an auth capability matrix by EOD. Priyom — can you book the sandbox for Thu 2027-03-25 10:00 PT?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
